text:
alex: heads up — seeing an SSE client hang after auth refresh in the JS SDK. stream stops emitting events for ~10s then a big coalesced chunk lands and the JSON parse fails. anyone seen this?
alex: repro (simple):
```
const evt = new EventSource(urlWithResumeToken);
// after token refresh we reconnect via new URL
```
but on reconnect we sometimes get two events merged: `data: {...}
data: {...}

` which our parser treats as one JSON blob.
maria: which sdk version? browser or node? any stack traces?
alex: node SDK 2.4.1 but same seen in browser 0.9.7. logs: 
```
stream: received fragment "data: {\"id\":1,\"msg\":\"a\"}\n\n"
stream: received fragment "data: {\"id\":2,\"msg\":\"b\"}\n\n"
parser: emit -> parse OK
parser: emit -> parse error: Unexpected token d in JSON at position 0
```
jordan: sounds like the reconnect path is not flushing the chunk boundary or the framing code merges adjacent 'data:' lines when resume happens. are you using the SDK's native parser or a custom one?
alex: native parser. I'm seeing cases where two fragments arrive in a single TCP packet and our streaming parser assumes a single `data:` block then tries JSON.parse on the whole chunk.
sam: this matches a bug I fixed in the runtime framing code last month — we only split on '\n\n' but sometimes heartbeat/newline normalization collapses boundaries. quick workaround: treat multiple `data:` occurrences inside a chunk as separate events before parsing. e.g. pseudo: 
```
const parts = chunk.split(/\n(?=data: )/g);
parts.forEach(p => handleEvent(p));
```
maria: can you paste the minimal failing chunk (raw bytes)? that will help confirm split heuristic.
alex: here — raw-ish: "data: {\"id\":1,\"msg\":\"a\"}\n\ndata: {\"id\":2,\"msg\":\"b\"}\n\n" — but sometimes we see "data: {..}\ndata: {..}\n" with no trailing blank line until next TCP packet.
jordan: yep — that means parser must be resilient to partial blank-line boundaries. parser should buffer until a full event (blank-line) is seen, but also not attempt to parse if it contains multiple `data:` sections — split first.
ci-bot: build/sdks-js #418 pipeline passed (sam/patch-evt-split)
sam: put up PR to split on `\n(?=data:)` and added tests for chunk-coalescing. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdks/pull/418 (small change)
alex: trying pr locally now... running stress harness, reconnecting ~2000 times. initial looks promising, much fewer parse errors. still one case where two chunks fused with an extra carriage return `\r\n\r` and our regex missed it.
sam: ok i'll update to normalize `\r\n` -> `\n` before split; and add a test for the CRLF variant. i'll include browser and node SDKs.
maria: please backport to 0.9.x branch for browser sample apps — onboarding hits customers.
sam: will do, patching both branches. rolling out to staged CDN now, will monitor logs for 24h.
ajex: thanks y'all, huge help. once staged looks good i'll merge to main and cut a patch release. :thumbsup:
alex: confirmed fixed in staging after CRLF normalization. closing from my side. :tada:
